title: Displacement magnitude
description: Essential: Student must calculate the correct displacement magnitude of 10 m using vector addition.

title: Displacement direction
description: Essential: Student must state the correct direction (approximately 53° from positive x-axis) using appropriate trigonometry.

title: Average velocity magnitude
description: Essential: Student must calculate the correct average velocity magnitude of 5 m/s using displacement and total time.

title: Vector vs. scalar distinction
description: Important: Student must recognize displacement is a vector while distance is scalar, and average velocity uses displacement not total distance.

title: Proper trigonometric application
description: Important: Student must correctly apply inverse tangent (tan⁻¹) to find the angle from the x and y components.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student maintains consistent units (meters, seconds, m/s, degrees) throughout calculations.

title: Confusing distance with displacement
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly uses total distance (14 m) instead of displacement magnitude (10 m) in calculations.

title: Incorrect angle quadrant
description: Pitfall: Student calculates angle from wrong axis (e.g., from y-axis instead of x-axis) or misplaces the angle in wrong quadrant.
